title: Environment placement
description: Schema for <env>/placement.yaml — adopter facts about node placement. `placement` maps the template's placement groups (pg-N) to provider failure domains: physical node names on on-prem providers, availability zones on AWS. `pools` overrides template node pools BY NAME with SHALLOW per-top-level-field replacement (the declared semantics): each field the override names replaces the template pool's field WHOLESALE — lists included, so overriding `taints` or `disks` restates the whole list. Fields the override omits are inherited (an override changing count inherits everything else). enabled: false drops a default pool — greppable, a visible decision rather than an absence; unknown names add extra pools and must carry the full pool shape. Rationale: list deep-merge is ambiguous for disks/taints; explicit wholesale replacement is legible.

placement.description: Placement group -> failure domain: a physical node name on on-prem providers (pg-1: pve-node-a), an availability zone on AWS (pg-1: eu-west-1a). On-prem, every pg-N the selected template references must be mapped; the plan fails otherwise. On AWS the file is optional (absent = best-effort ASG spread), but once present the same must-map rule applies.

pools.description: Per-pool overrides matched by name onto the template's node_groups. Semantics: shallow per-top-level-field replacement — a named field (count, cores, memory, disks, placement, tags, taints, class) replaces the template's field wholesale (lists are restated in full, never merged); omitted fields are inherited. enabled: false removes a pool. New names define extra pools and must then carry the full pool shape.
